name: Ferrospike
description: A vasodilating neuro-hydraulic compound that floods augment servo-lines and BCI motor pathways with a synthetic catecholamine analogue, temporarily pushing mechanical augments 40-70% beyond factory performance specifications. Myoelectric limbs strike harder, reflex rigs respond faster, and optical augments resolve detail at ranges they were never designed to reach. The body pays the price — joints, mounting points, and neural relay clusters sustain cumulative microdamage with each use.
effects: Mechanical augment output increased 40-70% beyond spec
Reflex augment response time reduced by up to 30ms
Optical augments gain extended zoom and low-light resolution
Subjective sense of physical invincibility and heightened aggression
Pain suppression at augment mounting points
side_effects: Micro-fractures in augment mounting hardware with repeated use
Neural relay burnout — permanent reflex degradation after 10+ uses
Hypertensive crisis risk in users with cardiac augments
Post-dose crash: 2-4 hours of muscle tremor and nausea
Servo fluid leak if augments are pushed past structural tolerance
Rare: complete mounting point shear under combat stress while spiked
cultural_context: Ferrospike is the combat drug of the Gray Zone. Pit fighters use it before sanctioned brawls. Gang enforcers take it before a job. It's cheap enough that Tier 1 workers with basic chrome pop it to meet brutal labor quotas that their stock-spec augments can't sustain. Medtechs in the Gray Zone call it 'eating your future' — every dose trades long-term augment integrity and neural health for short-term performance. A user who's been on Spike for a year has the mounting hardware of someone three times their age.
story_hooks: A Tier 1 pit fighter is found dead mid-match — not from opponent strikes but from a catastrophic mounting point shear at the shoulder that severed an artery. Someone sold them a batch cut with a compound that made the drug hit harder but degraded titanium bonding resin. Who's cutting it, and why?

A corporate security contractor is quietly purchasing Ferrospike in bulk — strange, given their salary could afford legitimate chrome enhancers. Someone is building a Spike-dependent fighting force that can be controlled by controlling their supply.

A the Gray Zone medtech has synthesized a variant they call 'Soft Spike' that gives 20% performance gains with zero hardware damage — but Nightshade Pharmatech is sending people to find them, because a safe version destroys the dependency model.
